experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r1-prefix-v1 target. Every trial runs steps 1 to 3 of the proof.md algorithm on a 1,088-byte message B and returns B with the 64-byte message A that the steps derive from it. Trial 0 uses the B of the first published pair of this construction (A comes out as the bytes 00..3f); trial 1 uses B = 1,088 zero bytes and is the algorithm's output, the certificate zero-b-pair; every other trial uses a B expanded from its organizer seed with SHAKE-256. Every trial is returned. The program evaluates the chunk compressions of B, not the target hash; the organizer recomputes both digests.
experiments.hypothesis: Every trial returns a 64-byte and a 1,088-byte message with equal complete 256-bit digests, as Lemma 1 and the theorem of proof.md Section 4 predict for every 1,088-byte B. The run checks that identity on concrete inputs; it is not evidence of attack cost, and no probability estimate is drawn from the seed expansion.
